issues.legal_issue: A High Court may examine in a second appeal whether the reasons for rejecting a will on grounds of suspicious circumstances are sustainable in law.
material_facts: The lower courts dismissed the suit based on a will, relying on its production only before trial and on reasons for disbelieving its attesting witnesses.
The High Court found no interpolation in the original will and held that the reasons for disbelieving the attesting witnesses were inadequate.
The High Court found the lower courts’ reasons for rejecting the will to be flimsy and allowed the second appeal.
issues.conclusion: The High Court rightly considered whether the lower courts’ reasons were sustainable; that issue amounted to a substantial question of law under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the High Court may consider whether the lower courts’ reasons for rejecting a will are sustainable in law. Although the propounder must establish valid execution and dispel suspicious circumstances to the court’s satisfaction, a substantial question of law arises when the lower courts reject the will on flimsy or legally unsustainable reasons. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.second_appeal_concerns_will_validity: The proceeding is a second appeal in which the validity of a will is in issue.
predicates.lower_courts_rejected_will_on_suspicious: The lower courts rejected a will because they considered circumstances surrounding it suspicious.
predicates.rejection_reasons_were_found_unsustainab: The High Court found the lower courts’ reasons for rejecting the will to be flimsy or otherwise unsustainable.

issues.definition: When a second appeal concerns the validity of a will rejected by the lower courts on suspicious circumstances, and the High Court finds their reasons unsustainable, reviewing those reasons raises a substantial question of law.
